blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Rank counts only communities with at least ten homes listed. Falling listings with steady sales mean homes are being absorbed faster; rising listings with steady sales mean more choice for buyers. A sellers’ best bet is a community where homes sell quickly against the number listed; a buyers’ best bet is the reverse. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Condo buildings in Matsqui Prairie
Streets, schools and getting around Matsqui Prairie

items.t: Matsqui Prairie is the rural, agricultural flat north of Abbotsford Centre, along the Fraser River, with Mission across the river to the north via Highway 11. The City's planning profile name is "Matsqui Prairie"; Matsqui Village, a historic rural centre, sits in the centre surrounded by agricultural land.
BC Geographical Names lists "Matsqui" as an official urban community in the City of Abbotsford.
Precise east and west boundary roads are not stated in the City profile text: Not confirmed.
Riverside Road runs through Matsqui Village; Matsqui Village Park is at 6074 Riverside Road, and Fire Hall No. 4 is at 5775 Wallace Street in the village.
Máthxwi Elementary is at 33661 Elizabeth Avenue.
BC Transit Route 31 (Abbotsford/Mission) serves the area — 31A trips stop at Matsqui Village, running between Bourquin Exchange and Mission City Station via Junction Mall.

Where condo stock actually concentrates: nowhere in Matsqui Prairie. There is no town centre, tower corridor or transit node with apartment condos here — the land pattern is A1 Agricultural and RR Rural Residential lots. SnapStats recorded attached (condos & townhomes) inventory of 0 and solds of 0 for Matsqui in September 2026.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Matsqui Prairie

items.t: Form B — Information Certificate (Strata Property Act, s.59): The seller's strata must provide a Form B stating the monthly strata fee, any special levy already approved, the contingency reserve fund (CRF) balance, parking/storage entitlements and any judgments or proceedings; since April 1, 2023 the Form B must also include a summary of the strata's insurance coverage.
CRF minimum contribution: Effective November 1, 2023, when approving budgets at the AGM, strata corporations must contribute a minimum of 10% of the annual operating fund to the CRF.
55+ bylaws (ss.123.1/123.2): The only age bylaw a strata may still have is 55+; exemptions expanded May 1, 2023 cover younger spouses/partners, caregivers, and children in defined cases.

Abbotsford zoning / OCP: Zoning Bylaw 2400 (2014) governs land use. The city-wide plan is Abbotsforward 2050, Official Community Plan Bylaw 2600-2016 (as updated), whose rural-centres policy recognizes Matsqui Village among Abbotsford's seven historical rural centres.

Property transfer tax (PTT): General rates are 1% on the first $200,000, 2% to $2M and 3% above, plus 2% on residential value above $3M. The first-time buyer exemption covers tax on the first $500,000 (max saving $8,000) for homes up to $835,000, with a partial exemption to $860,000 and none at/above $860,000. The separate Newly Built Home Exemption is full to $1,100,000 and phases out at $1,150,000.
HBP / FHSA: The RRSP Home Buyers' Plan allows $60,000 per person; the First Home Savings Account allows $8,000 per year to a $40,000 lifetime limit.
Mortgage insurance: CMHC states premium rates range from 0.6% to 4.5% of the total mortgage amount, and insurance is required when the down payment is less than 20% on a home priced $1.5M or less.

Local tax wrinkle specific to the prairie: properties in the Matsqui Prairie Dyking District pay a separate dyking district levy on top of general municipal rates, per the City's 2026 Tax Rates Summary under Tax Rates Bylaw No. 3727-2026.

blocks.text: Good to know about Matsqui Prairie

items.t: The prairie's plan status protects the current form. Abbotsforward 2050 (OCP Bylaw 2600-2016, as updated) recognizes Matsqui Village under its rural-centres policy as one of seven historical rural centres — there is no neighbourhood plan designating the prairie for apartment development in any source checked.

AgRefresh changed farm rules, not housing form. The City's agricultural review led to OCP Amendment Bylaw 3247-2022 and Zoning Bylaw Amendment Bylaw 3246-2022 — agricultural policy, not a condo or multi-family rezoning of the prairie.
No presale or new-construction condo project in Matsqui Prairie was verified on a City development page or developer site in the Nov 1, 2026 research.
Abbotsford tax dates changed the penalty pattern buyers may remember: taxes were due July 2, 2026, with a 5% penalty July 3, 2026 and a second 5% penalty September 16, 2026.

The nearest recreation and library are outside the sub-area — Matsqui Recreation Centre, 3106 Clearbrook Road, and Clearbrook Library, 32320 George Ferguson Way — which is the practical reality behind the "no condo stock" finding: services cluster south of the prairie, not in it.

Provincial strata changes that would apply to any future strata here: the 10% minimum CRF contribution (Nov 1, 2023), Form B insurance summaries (Apr 1, 2023), void rental bylaws and 55+-only age bylaws (Nov 24, 2022), and five-year depreciation-report renewal.

blocks.text: Townhome complexes in Matsqui
Streets, schools and getting around Matsqui

items.t: Abbotsford community medians (Matsqui medians are not published: Not verified at sub-area level): detached $949,000; attached $497,500, $433/sq ft, 97% sale-to-list, 32 days on market.
Where the townhouse stock concentrates: nowhere in Matsqui Prairie.

Schools (SD34; Ministry-listed names only): the school physically inside the sub-area is Mathxwí Elementary School, 33661 Elizabeth Ave, Abbotsford — renamed from Matsqui Elementary; SD34 records that Mathxwí refers to an area that can easily be portaged with one's canoe. Catchments are set by home address through the SD34 School Locator; the recorded locator run for 33661 Elizabeth Ave (the school's own address) returns: Elementary = Máthxwí Elementary; Middle = Clayburn Middle; Secondary = Robert Bateman Secondary — that address only; catchments for every other Matsqui address stay not verified. The district's feeder pattern supports the chain: Clayburn Middle lists Mathxwi among its feeder elementaries, and Clayburn's family of schools is headed by Robert Bateman Secondary.

Village anchors: Matsqui Village Park, 6074 Riverside Road; Fire Hall No. 4, 5775 Wallace Street in Matsqui Village; Matsqui Trail Regional Park provides walking and cycling trails along the Fraser River dyke — an FVRD regional park maintained and operated by the City of Abbotsford. The nearest City recreation complex (Matsqui Recreation Centre / MRC Sports Complex, 3106 Clearbrook Road) and the nearest library (Clearbrook Library, 32320 George Ferguson Way) are both outside the sub-area. Transit: BC Transit Route 31 (Abbotsford/Mission) serves the sub-area — 31A trips stop at Matsqui Village, between Bourquin Exchange and Mission City Station via Junction Mall. Driving commute times: Not verified.

Health: Abbotsford Regional Hospital and Cancer Centre, 32900 Marshall Road, Abbotsford (24/7, emergency, surgery and maternity); Mission Memorial Hospital across the Fraser River in Mission (24/7 emergency stabilization); Abbotsford Urgent and Primary Care Centre, 100-2692 Clearbrook Road.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Matsqui

items.t: Fee-simple reality — the core position here: Matsqui homes are fee-simple freehold farm and rural-residential properties. For a fee-simple home there is no strata, no Form B and no strata fees — municipal rules (Zoning Bylaw 2400-2014), ALR rules where the parcel is in the ALR, and any registered covenants only.

If a strata townhouse is bought elsewhere in Abbotsford — the BC standard block: Form B diligence (Strata Property Act s. 123.1/123.2 + Regulation 7.01, exemptions expanded May 1, 2023 for a younger spouse/partner, live-in caregivers, legacy residents and defined children).

ALR housing frame (the prairie's actual density rules): under ALC housing rules, ALR land may generally have no more than one residence per parcel; the principal residence is capped at 500 m² total floor area; a secondary suite is permitted only within the principal residence; and an additional residence is capped at 90 m² (parcels ≤40 ha) or 186 m² (parcels >40 ha). In the A1 zone specifically: one Accessory Farm Dwelling Unit per lot only under the ALR Use Regulation, B.C. Reg. 30/2019, or as approved by the ALC, on a lot of at least 0.4 ha, capped at 90 m² / 186 m² by lot size, plus one secondary suite per lot to 100 m². In the RR zone: a coach house only on a lot greater than 0.4 ha, with a coach house or suite limited to one per lot and the lesser of 90 m² or 40% of the principal dwelling's net floor area. None of these creates a separate title for sale.

Farm-class thresholds (full three-tier form): $2,500 of farm income for parcels of 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 plus 5% of the value of land over 4 ha for larger parcels; $10,000 for parcels under 0.8 ha; applications by October 31.

Flood, dykes and the dyking levy: the City states the Matsqui Dykes are designed to prevent Fraser River water from entering Matsqui Prairie — design protection is not a parcel-level guarantee; confirm flood status with the City for the specific lot. Properties in the Matsqui Prairie Dyking District pay a separate dyking district levy on top of general municipal rates, per the City's 2026 Tax Rates Summary under Tax Rates Bylaw No. 3727-2026. Abbotsford property taxes were due July 2, 2026 by midnight, with a first 5% penalty on July 3, 2026 and a second 5% penalty on September 16, 2026 (the City's Matsqui-relevant schedule — note the second-penalty date is September 16 on the City's notice page, not a generic September date). Wells and septic: rural properties rely on wells (recorded in the provincial GWELLS database) and onsite sewage systems (Fraser Health authorized-person filings before and after work); servicing for any individual property: Not verified.

The recreation centre named for this area is not in this area. Matsqui Recreation Centre and the MRC Sports Complex are at 3106 Clearbrook Road in Clearbrook, and the nearest library is Clearbrook Library, 32320 George Ferguson Way — services cluster south of the prairie, which is the practical reality behind the zero-townhouse finding.

The dyke is also the recreation. Matsqui Trail Regional Park runs walking and cycling trails along the Fraser River dyke — an FVRD regional park maintained and operated by the City of Abbotsford — so the flood infrastructure doubles as the sub-area's main park amenity.
"Matsqui" names three different things. Searches blend all three, and only the first two are in Abbotsford.

What trades here

items.t: Fee-simple farm parcels are the land form — and nearly the whole market

Lot character — set by the rural zones, not by a subdivision pattern: in the A1 Agricultural Zone (Zoning Bylaw No. 2400-2014, s.210), parcels created through subdivision must be a minimum of 8.0 ha; in the RR Rural Residential Zone (s.310), intended for single detached dwellings and agricultural uses on large lots in a rural setting, the minimum lot size is 4.0 ha.

: A bare-land strata lot, where the form lawfully exists elsewhere, is strata tenure — Form B, strata fees and bylaws apply to the lot. Any strata claim for a Matsqui address is not confirmed until a strata plan is produced.
: the seven cards read include one Land card (a producing blueberry farm per its listing text) and one bare-lot card with institutional zoning described in its listing text.

The dyked prairie — the land's defining physical fact: The City states that the Matsqui Dykes are designed to prevent water in the Fraser River from entering into Matsqui Prairie, and Matsqui Trail Regional Park runs along the Fraser River dyke. Design protection is not a parcel-level guarantee: the flood status of a specific parcel is a City confirmation, not an assumption.
Servicing — wells and onsite sewage: Servicing for any individual property: Not verified — read the GWELLS record and the sewerage filings for the parcel before pricing it.

ALR: the prairie's agricultural policy frame is the Agricultural Land Reserve as administered through the City's AgRefresh review, which led to OCP Amendment Bylaw 3247-2022 and Zoning Bylaw Amendment Bylaw 3246-2022. The A1/RR zoning and the ALC housing rules are the prairie's governing set. A parcel-by-parcel ALR determination for a specific Matsqui property is not confirmed until the ALC map and title are read for that parcel, so a buyer should underwrite every prairie parcel as ALR-framed until that check says otherwise.

Named subdivisions / bare-land developments: none verified: No presale or new-construction project in Matsqui was verified on a City development page or a developer site: Not verified. Matsqui Village itself is a historic rural centre recognized in the OCP's rural-centres policy — a village of existing parcels, not a lot development.

items.t: The page is headed "Matsqui Abbotsford Homes for Sale | MLS | Jared Gibbons." Its editorial works to Highway 11 (the Abbotsford-Mission Highway), Harris Road, Beharrell Road, Foreman Road, Gladwin Road North, Page Road and Riverside Road toward the Mission Bridge, describing ALR farm parcels across Matsqui Prairie, country residences along Harris Road, character homes in historic Matsqui Village near Foreman Road, and rural view properties looking north to Mission.

City name for the same ground: the City of Abbotsford's planning profile name is "Matsqui Prairie"; Matsqui Village, a historic rural centre, sits in the centre of the prairie surrounded by agricultural land. BC Geographical Names lists "Matsqui" as an official urban community in the City of Abbotsford. Where it sits: north of Abbotsford Centre along the Fraser River, with the Fraser River on its north side; precise east and west boundary roads are not stated in the City profile text: Not verified.
Individual card prices are feed data, not stated as market facts here.

School physically inside the sub-area: Mathxwí Elementary School, 33661 Elizabeth Ave, Abbotsford — renamed from Matsqui Elementary; SD34 records that Mathxwí refers to an area that can easily be portaged with one's canoe. Catchments are set by home address through the SD34 School Locator; the recorded locator run for 33661 Elizabeth Ave (the school's own address, settled in the SD34 Abbotsford run) returns Elementary = Mathxwí Elementary, Middle = Clayburn Middle, Secondary = Robert Bateman Secondary — that address only; catchments for every other Matsqui address stay not verified.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Matsqui

items.t: : The OCP's rural-centres policy recognizes the role of Abbotsford's seven historical rural centres, which include Matsqui Village.

Zoning — A1 Agricultural Zone (Zoning Bylaw No. 2400-2014, s.210): Agricultural Use and Single Detached Dwelling are principal uses; parcels created through subdivision must be a minimum of 8.0 ha; one Accessory Farm Dwelling Unit is permitted per lot only in accordance with the Agricultural Land Reserve Use Regulation, B.C. Reg. 30/2019, or as approved by the Agricultural Land Commission, on a lot of at least 0.4 ha, with a maximum floor area of 90 m² on lots of 40 ha or less and 186 m² on lots over 40 ha; one secondary suite per lot is permitted, to a maximum floor area of 100 m².

Zoning — RR Rural Residential Zone (s.310): intended for single detached dwellings and agricultural uses on large lots in a rural setting; minimum lot size 4.0 ha; a coach house is permitted only on a lot greater than 0.4 ha, and a coach house or secondary suite is limited to one per lot and a maximum floor area of 90 m² or 40% of the net floor area of the single detached dwelling, whichever is less.

SSMUH (Abbotsford): the SSMUH bylaw number is not confirmed, so none is stated. The Abbotsford Development (servicing) Bylaw number is likewise not confirmed, so no bylaw number is stated for it. Subdivision runs against the A1/RR minimums above and the City's development process; confirm with the City per parcel.

ALR block (the prairie's governing frame, parcel by parcel): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)); caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class is three-tier — $2,500 on 0.8–4 ha / $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha / $10,000 under 0.8 ha, applications by Oct 31 — a flat "$2,500+" line is an error, and no farm-class claim is asserted for any specific Matsqui parcel.

Flood / dyking diligence: the City states the Matsqui Dykes are designed to prevent Fraser River water from entering Matsqui Prairie; properties in the Matsqui Prairie Dyking District pay a separate dyking district levy on top of general municipal rates, per the City's 2026 Tax Rates Summary (Tax Rates Bylaw No. 3727-2026). Protection design is not a guarantee for a specific parcel — confirm the parcel's flood status with the City, and check the tax notice for the dyking levy line item.

blocks.text: Good to know about Matsqui

items.t: The village school's name changed — the page's did not. Mathxwí Elementary (33661 Elizabeth Ave) was renamed from Matsqui Elementary; SD34 records that Mathxwí refers to an area that can easily be portaged with one's canoe.
The page's second school address is unconfirmed too.

The dyking levy is a Matsqui-only line item. Properties in the Matsqui Prairie Dyking District pay a separate levy on top of general municipal rates, shown in the City's 2026 Tax Rates Summary — a carrying cost an Abbotsford buyer from outside the district will not have seen on another Abbotsford tax notice.
The name trap outside the sub-area. Likewise the Matsqui Recreation Centre (3106 Clearbrook Road) carries the name but sits in Clearbrook, outside the sub-area.

History in the name itself. BC Geographical Names records that Matsqui is named after a tribe of the Halkomaylem division who lived on the lower Fraser River and Sumas Lake, that the name's origin is the Halq'eméylem (Salishan) language, and that the first settler on Matsqui Prairie arrived at a point called "Saw-aqum," meaning "wild celery."
Small counts make this sub-area's headline ratio a signal, not a trend. (SnapStats FVR September 2026 report)

blocks.text: Acreage and rural land in Matsqui Prairie

The acreage in Matsqui Prairie is farm land: fee-simple agricultural parcels on a dyked river prairie, in the A1 Agricultural Zone (subdivision minimum 8.0 ha) and the RR Rural Residential Zone (minimum lot size 4.0 ha). This is the one ground in this group where an acreage market genuinely exists — and it trades as whole farm parcels, not as a named acreage subdivision product.
The ground in Matsqui Prairie

items.t: ALR vs non-ALR split: The prairie's agricultural policy frame is the Agricultural Land Reserve as administered through the City's AgRefresh review, which led to OCP Amendment Bylaw 3247-2022 and Zoning Bylaw Amendment Bylaw 3246-2022.
Serviced vs unserviced ground: Servicing for any individual property: Not verified — read the GWELLS record and the sewerage filings for the parcel before pricing it.
Any strata claim for a Matsqui address is not confirmed until a strata plan is produced.

Named acreage subdivisions / developments: none verified: Matsqui Village itself is a historic rural centre recognized in the OCP's rural-centres policy — a village of existing parcels, not an acreage development.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect acreage buyers in Matsqui Prairie

items.t: Zoning: Abbotsford Zoning Bylaw No. 2400-2014, rural sections: A1 Agricultural Zone (s.210): Agricultural Use and Single Detached Dwelling are principal uses; parcels created through subdivision must be a minimum of 8.0 ha; one Accessory Farm Dwelling Unit is permitted per lot only in accordance with the ALR Use Regulation, B.C. Reg. 30/2019, or as approved by the Agricultural Land Commission, on a lot of at least 0.4 ha, with a maximum floor area of 90 m² on lots of 40 ha or less and 186 m² on lots over 40 ha; one secondary suite per lot is permitted, to a maximum floor area of 100 m². RR Rural Residential Zone (s.310): minimum lot size 4.0 ha; a coach house is permitted only on a lot greater than 0.4 ha, and a coach house or secondary suite is limited to one per lot and a maximum floor area of 90 m² or 40% of the net floor area of the single detached dwelling, whichever is less. None of these added dwellings creates a separate title for sale.

The dyking levy: Abbotsford property tax is the BC Assessment value multiplied by a rate per $1,000 of net assessed value set under the Tax Rates Bylaw No. 3727-2026, and the City's 2026 Tax Rates Summary lists a separate Matsqui Prairie Dyking District levy charged on properties in the district, on top of the general municipal rates. Check the parcel's tax notice for the line item — two otherwise identical prairie parcels can carry different bills if only one sits in the district.

Flood diligence: The Matsqui Dykes are designed to keep Fraser River water out of the prairie — a design statement by the City, not a guarantee for a specific parcel. Ask about flood history directly, confirm the parcel's flood status with the City, and read the dyking levy as the ongoing price of the protection system.

Strata block — redirect case only: None of the BC strata block applies to a Matsqui fee-simple parcel purchase itself. If a strata purchase is made elsewhere in Abbotsford: Form B diligence; depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws void since November 24, 2022; only 55+ age bylaws valid (SPA ss. 123.1/123.2, May 1, 2023 exemptions) — a "45+" listing line is not a valid BC age bylaw.

blocks.text: Good to know about Matsqui Prairie

items.t: The recreation centre named for this area is not in this area: Matsqui Recreation Centre (MRC Sports Complex) is at 3106 Clearbrook Road in Clearbrook, and the nearest library is Clearbrook Library, 32320 George Ferguson Way — the prairie's services cluster south of it, which is part of why no lot product has ever formed here.

The dyke is also the park: Matsqui Trail Regional Park provides walking and cycling trails along the Fraser River dyke — a Fraser Valley Regional District regional park maintained and operated by the City of Abbotsford. The flood infrastructure a prairie buyer pays the levy for doubles as the sub-area's main recreation amenity.

The village school carries the prairie's history in its name: Mathxwí Elementary (33661 Elizabeth Avenue) was renamed from Matsqui Elementary; SD34 records that Mathxwí refers to an area that can easily be portaged with one's canoe, and BC Geographical Names records the first settler on Matsqui Prairie arriving at a point called "Saw-aqum," meaning "wild celery." The correct current school name is Mathxwí Elementary — pages using the old name as a current name are dated.

What a duplex looks like in Matsqui Prairie

blocks.text: Local rules that affect duplexes in Matsqui Prairie

items.t: ALR housing (governs most prairie parcels): Land in the ALR may generally have no more than one residence per parcel unless the owner qualifies for an additional residence; the principal residence must be 500 m² or less in total floor area; a secondary suite is permitted in the ALR only within the principal residence; and an additional detached residence may be up to 90 m² on properties of 40 ha or less and 186 m² on properties over 40 ha. Subdivision within the ALR requires Agricultural Land Commission approval.

Flood and dykes: The City states the Matsqui Dykes are designed to prevent water in the Fraser River from entering into Matsqui Prairie; properties in the Matsqui Prairie Dyking District pay a separate dyking district levy on top of general municipal rates, per the City's 2026 Tax Rates Summary (Tax Rates Bylaw No. 3727-2026). Protection design is not a parcel-level guarantee — confirm a specific parcel's flood status with the City.

faq.q: Can I actually buy a condo in Matsqui Prairie?
faq.a: No verified apartment-condo building exists in the sub-area — attached inventory and sales were both 0 in September 2026, and the zoning is agricultural/rural-residential single-detached.

faq.q: If a strata unit appeared here, what would strata fees cover?
faq.a: That is set by that strata's budget and disclosed on the Form B (s.59), which must state the monthly fee, CRF balance and, since April 1, 2023, a summary of insurance coverage. There is no Matsqui building whose fee/coverage can be quoted: Not confirmed.

faq.q: Could I rent out a strata unit here?
faq.a: Provincially, long-term rental-restriction bylaws have been void since November 24, 2022; a strata can still restrict short-term rentals.

Pet bylaws were not removed by the 2022 changes — they remain building-by-building in the strata's bylaws, disclosed with the Form B package. With no verified building here, any specific pet rule is not confirmed.

faq.q: How do I judge a building's finances?
faq.a: Read the Form B for the CRF balance and approved levies, and the depreciation report for major-item timing; stratas with 5+ lots in the FVRD without a report had to obtain one by July 1, 2026, and must now contribute at least 10% of the operating fund to the CRF each year.

faq.q: Can I actually buy a townhouse in Matsqui Prairie?
faq.a: No verified townhouse complex — strata or fee-simple — exists in the sub-area: attached inventory and sales were both 0 in September 2026, the zoning is agricultural/rural-residential single-detached (A1 minimum 8.0 ha; RR minimum 4.0 ha), and ALR residences cannot be stratified.

faq.q: Why are there no townhouses — could a developer build some?
faq.a: The minimum lot sizes alone block the form, most parcels sit in or beside the ALR, and the ALR stratification bar (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; SPA s. 239; ALCA s. 21(1)) prevents a farm property from becoming strata townhouse lots. No townhouse rezoning or project was verified in any source checked.

faq.q: What do I get instead of a townhouse here?
faq.a: A fee-simple detached farm or rural-residential home: no strata fees, no Form B, no strata bylaws — instead zoning, ALR rules, well and septic diligence, and the Matsqui Prairie Dyking District levy on the tax bill.

faq.q: What acreage can I actually buy on Matsqui Prairie?
faq.a: A whole fee-simple farm parcel (A1 zone) or a large rural-residential parcel (RR zone). There is no named acreage subdivision, no bare-land strata, no strata of any kind and no presale acreage product — the strata zero is structural (ALR residences cannot be stratified, and the subdivision minimums are 8.0 ha and 4.0 ha).

faq.q: Can I split a prairie parcel for my kids or to sell a lot?
faq.a: Only if the math survives: A1 parcels created by subdivision must be at least 8.0 ha and RR lots at least 4.0 ha, and subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval on top.

faq.q: What second dwelling can go on an A1 lot?
faq.a: One Accessory Farm Dwelling Unit per lot, only via the ALR Use Regulation (B.C. Reg. 30/2019) or ALC approval, on a lot of at least 0.4 ha, capped at 90 m² (lots of 40 ha or less) or 186 m² (over 40 ha) — plus one secondary suite per lot to 100 m² under the zone, subject on ALR land to the ALC rule that a suite sits only within the principal residence. In the RR zone: one coach house or suite on a lot over 0.4 ha, at the lesser of 90 m² or 40% of the main house. None of these creates a separate saleable title.

faq.q: What does the dyking levy mean for my tax bill?
faq.a: Properties in the Matsqui Prairie Dyking District pay a separate levy on top of general municipal rates (Tax Rates Bylaw No. 3727-2026; 2026 Tax Rates Summary). It is a permanent holding-cost line for district parcels — confirm whether the parcel is in the district and read the line on its tax notice before comparing two prairie parcels on price alone.

faq.q: Can I buy a half duplex in Matsqui Prairie?
faq.a: What trades is fee-simple detached farm and rural-residential housing.

faq.q: Could I create a strata half duplex out of a prairie house?
faq.a: Not on ALR land — ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; alca s.21(1)). And a fee-simple split runs into the subdivision minimums first: 8.0 ha in A1, 4.0 ha in RR.

faq.q: What second units CAN a prairie lot carry?
faq.a: In A1: One secondary suite to 100 m², and one Accessory Farm Dwelling Unit through the ALR Use Regulation or ALC approval on a lot of at least 0.4 ha (90 m² / 186 m² by lot size). In RR: One coach house or suite on a lot over 0.4 ha, at the lesser of 90 m² or 40% of the principal dwelling. Abbotsford's general suite cap is under 50%, and its coach/garden cap is 15% of lot area to 100 m². Every unit stays on the one title.

faq.q: Is flood risk part of buying here?
faq.a: Yes. The Matsqui Dykes are designed to keep Fraser River water out of the prairie and district properties pay the separate dyking levy — design protection is not a guarantee for a specific parcel, so confirm flood status with the City for the lot.
